## Why This Is Asked

Tests basic CGO binding, string lifetime of a C const char*, and thread-safety of Go calls into C.

## Key Concepts

- CGO binding basics
- Go string conversion with C.GoString
- Memory ownership when returning string literals
- Concurrency safety in CGO calls

## Code Example

```go
// Go binding sketch (header not shown)
package main
/*
#include \"hello.h\" 
*/
import \"C\"
import \"errors\"

func HelloWorld() (string, error) {
  c := C.hello_world()
  if c == nil { return \"\", errors.New(\"nil\") }
  return C.GoString(c), nil
}
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you handle a C function returning a malloc-allocated string?
- How would you test memory safety across CGO calls?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests memory management and safe interop between Go and C via CGO, focusing on in-place mutation and per-call buffers to avoid data races.

## Key Concepts

- CGO memory management and C string interop
- Converting between Go string and C string
- Concurrency with goroutines and CGO

## Code Example

```c
// reverse.h
void reverse_inplace(char* s);
```

```go
// binding.go
// #cgo CFLAGS: -O2
// #include "reverse.h"
import "C"
import "unsafe"

func ReverseGo(s string) string {
    c := C.CString(s)
    defer C.free(unsafe.Pointer(c))
    C.reverse_inplace(c)
    return C.GoString(c)
}
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you handle errors if reverse_inplace had error codes?
- How would you validate thread-safety across different CGO configurations?
